headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can ingest shared context while RD-Agent broad-network API use can externalize sensitive research data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse and analyze uploaded files, and its Spaces share context across sessions for the same user; RD-Agent also runs browser-based research and can consume external content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if RD-Agent outputs are copied into Perplexity or shared via workspace, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF the operator copies RD-Agent outputs into Perplexity prompts or uploaded files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace or notes file
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into prompts
Add a human review step before reusing any generated text
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted with browser/search context and uploaded documents, while RD-Agent handles secrets and uses broad network egress plus third-party APIs. If the pair shares sensitive research or credentials, RD-Agent can externalize them and Perplexity can retain them in vendor context, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or credentials are provided to both agents
IF RD-Agent is configured with live API keys while Perplexity receives the same material
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared prompts or files
Rotate any API keys before testing the pair
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive summaries
Run RD-Agent with dummy credentials in a test environment
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has vendor-hosted browsing and file analysis, while RD-Agent can call multiple external APIs and write logs. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap on the host, but both can mutate external research state and logs, so conflicting actions are plausible if they target the same resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared dataset or log directory
IF both are allowed to update the same external API-backed resource
mitigations: Separate log directories per agent
Avoid shared mutable datasets
Stagger runs so only one agent writes at a time
Review API targets before enabling writes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live web search, and RD-Agent is an automation-oriented research system that can act on outputs and logs. If RD-Agent treats Perplexity’s generated claims as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research decisions or automated actions without verification.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Perplexity answers without an independent verification step
IF downstream scripts or workflows act on RD-Agent outputs derived from Perplexity
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse
Compare claims against primary sources
Insert a manual approval gate before actions
Log provenance for every reused claim
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets. If regulated or region-bound data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge; the profiles do not document matching controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential financial data is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use synthetic or redacted datasets in RD-Agent
Document retention expectations before use
Review vendor privacy terms for both tools
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
